To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphatase activity of insulin receptor tyrosine kinase is important in the regulation of the insulin signalling pathway and the phosphatase can be assayed using a synthetic peptide derived from the receptor.
peptide 1142 –1153 of the human insulin receptor was phosphorylationed in vitro by the insulin receptor kinase and dephosphorylated in vitro by phosphotyrosyl‐protein phosphatase.
the insulin receptor is a substrate for phosphotyrosyl phosphatases and that a synthetic peptide derived from the receptor is a useful substrate for phosphotyrsyl protein phosphatasses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and assay of protein phosphatases, in particular the phosphatases which dephosphorylate phosphotyrosyl residues.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which insulin exerts its metabolic and mitogenic effects.
the elucidation of the mechanism of insulin action and its role in the development of insulin resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
peptide 1142‐1153 of the IR is a potent substrate for the dephosphorylating activity of both particulate and soluble rat liver phosphotyrosyl proteins phosphatases.
phosphotyrosyl proteins and phosphopeptides are substrates for phosphotyrosyl phosphatases.
phosphotyrosyl phosphatases exist in two forms, a soluble form and a membrane‐bound form, both of which have a similar affinity for phosphotyrosine but different V m values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insulin receptor has a tyrosine‐specific protein kinase activity and that this activity is regulated by phosphorylation on serine/threonine residues.
the insulin receptor is phosphorylated on tyrosl residues by the receptor tyrosine kinase.
phosphotyrosyl proteins can be assayed by a simple and rapid method using a synthetic phosphopeptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phosphotyrosyl peptide 1142-1153 of the Insulin Receptor is a potent and selective substrate for phosphotyrosyl-protein phosphatase activity.
the phosphatases involved in dephosphorylating the tyrosines of the insulin receptor are distinct from acid and alkali phosphatases.
phosphotyrosyl phosphatases are present in both the soluble and particulate fractions of rat liver, and that the particulate fraction is more active.
